purpose: Challenge one canonical link-only associative-string topology above the exact [bbbbbbbb] byte transport while preserving the distinction between canonical source content, exact source occurrence and dictionary-resolved form.

byteLayer.byteCarrierLink: B = fold(R, [ open, bit0..bit7, close ]) over exact R/O/C/L/U abit refs

candidateA.name: nested-byte-history-with-source-occurrence
candidateA.content: C = fold(R, canonical byte refs in source order)
candidateA.reason: byte boundaries remain explicit subrelations, identical byte content has one reusable lexical key, and repeated source occurrences remain distinguishable without a host string/list object

candidateB.name: flat-abit-history
candidateB.shape: fold(R, every physical abit of concatenated [bbbbbbbb] carriers)
candidateB.concern: it flattens the already-established byte carrier level, so string sequencing is not expressed over explicit byte relations and source occurrence remains conflated with canonical content

requiredAssertions: all 256 bytes have distinct canonical link carriers and round-trip through exact [bbbbbbbb] topology
arbitrary byte sequences round-trip through a nested byte-history content carrier
empty content is represented by the exact R protocol seed while an empty source occurrence remains a distinct self-closed link
prefix strings such as A and AB have different canonical content refs
the immediate sequence elements are canonical byte refs rather than flattened physical abits
the same byte sequence reconstructed twice reuses one canonical content ref inside one exact-pair network
two source occurrences over that same content are exact-occurrence-distinct
dictionary lookup keys canonical content so two same-content occurrences can reuse one entry without erasing occurrence identity
same Unicode appearance with distinct UTF-8 bytes remains distinct when caller supplies distinct bytes
invalid UTF-8 remains representable as byte content and fails only at strict text decode
malformed byte histories, non-byte string elements and cyclic string histories reject finitely
source occurrence role is explicit in the act/context and is not inferred from self-closed shape
flat-abit history remains round-trippable historical scaffold but is not selected as canonical astring topology
no Link gains string/content/type/address metadata and no production parser/interpreter changes

decisionCandidate.wording: An associative string has canonical byte content represented by an R-seeded history of canonical [bbbbbbbb] byte-link carriers. A concrete source occurrence is a separate self-closed link S=S⟼C. Lexical dictionaries key canonical content C; interpretation acts carry the exact S occurrence when occurrence identity matters.

notDecided: production API/module names for astring values
whether occurrence-specific source relations are exposed in surface syntax
tokenization of multi-glyph formal notation above astring content
